result.title: Sufficient Frame Subsets for Video Understanding
result.summary: Understanding when during a video a model makes its critical observations is essential for interpreting video-understanding systems. However, existing attribution methods often spread evidence diffusely across near-duplicate frames. We introduce Sufficient Frame Subsets: compact sets of frames in which all other frames are masked, yet each subset independently preserves the model's prediction. We evaluate our method on two complementary benchmarks, UCF101 and Something-Something v2, using both CNN- and transformer-based architectures. Our results show that the proposed algorithm identifies highly compact and effective frame subsets for explaining model decisions. We also find that models capable of relying on a greater number of sufficient frame subsets tend to perform better, possibly because they are more robust, consistent with prior research. Finally, the extracted frame subsets help us analyze model failure cases, reveal which aspects of a video the model has learned to emphasize, and identify opportunities for improving future training procedures.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Sufficient Frame Subsets：在掩码其余帧的条件下，搜索能独立保持模型预测的紧凑帧子集，并在 UCF101、Something-Something v2 上用 CNN 与 Transformer 架构评估其解释效果与失败案例分析价值。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「最小充分证据子集」的掩码搜索与预测保持这一充分性判据，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、以及 LOOK/STOP 是否已获取足够信息的判定提供可核查的方法线索；但研究对象是视频分类归因而非多模态推理，迁移需另行设计。
